title: Persona Prompting as a Lens on LLM Social Reasoning

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs with age-specific personas (e.g., 15, 35, 65 years old) and comparing classification and rationale agreement against ground-truth annotations from different age demographics (Young vs. Old).
Prompting LLMs with gender-specific personas (Male, Female) and measuring variations in task performance, label prediction, and token-level rationale extraction.
Prompting models with race-specific personas (White, Black, Asian) and evaluating output alignment with annotations from specific human demographic groups (African American, Hispanic, Caucasian).
Conditioning LLMs with religious personas (Christian, Muslim, Jewish, Atheist, Hindu) to assess how generated labels and rationales for hate speech detection vary across affiliations.

Simulating personas with varying education levels (No formal education, High school, Higher education) to analyze differences in label prediction and the linguistic complexity of chain-of-thought rationales.

Applying political personas (Left-wing, Right-wing, Centrist) and measuring inter-persona agreement, classification shifts, and rationale selection in socially sensitive tasks like hate speech detection.
Prompting models with social connectedness traits (Not lonely, Somewhat lonely) to evaluate differences in sensitivity and interpretation of potentially offensive or ambiguous text.
